gold.question: Under the original text of Directive (EU) 2019/771, for how long is a seller liable for a lack of conformity that already exists when the goods are delivered? May a Member State provide a longer period, and may the period be shorter for second-hand goods?
gold.reference_answer: The seller is liable where that lack of conformity becomes apparent within two years of delivery. Without prejudice to Article 7(3), that rule also applies to goods with digital elements. Member States may maintain or introduce longer time limits than those in Article 10(1) and (2). For second-hand goods, Member States may allow the seller and the consumer to agree a shorter liability or limitation period than those in paragraphs 1, 2 and 5, but that shorter period must not be less than one year.
key_facts: 1. The seller shall be liable to the consumer for any lack of conformity which exists at the time when the goods were delivered and which becomes apparent within two years of that time. Without prejudice to Article 7(3), this paragraph shall also apply to goods with digital elements.
3. Member States may maintain or introduce longer time limits than those referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.

6. Member States may provide that, in the case of second-hand goods, the seller and the consumer can agree to contractual terms or agreements with a shorter liability or limitation period than those referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 5, provided that such shorter periods shall not be less than one year.

evidence.text: 1. The seller shall be liable to the consumer for any lack of conformity which exists at the time when the goods were delivered and which becomes apparent within two years of that time. Without prejudice to Article 7(3), this paragraph shall also apply to goods with digital elements.

6.
